about: Capitals, main languages and a fun fact for every place on the map, and capital, nickname and fun fact for every US state, written by hand for Country Quest (checked October 2026). Keys are the codes in countries.json and us-states.json. 'capital' and 'languages' can be a list; a missing 'capital' means the place has none. 'pop' fills in a population the map data lacks (for the states: the 2020 census).

AFG.fact: Afghanistan has no coast at all, and the snowy Hindu Kush mountains run right across the middle of it.

ALB.fact: In Albania, a nod of the head can mean 'no' and a shake can mean 'yes': the opposite of many countries!

DZA.fact: Algeria is the biggest country in Africa, and most of it is covered by the Sahara Desert.

AND.fact: Andorra is a tiny country high in the Pyrenees mountains. Its capital is the highest in Europe.

AGO.fact: The giant sable antelope, with huge curved horns, lives only in Angola. It is the country's national symbol.

ATG.fact: Antigua is said to have 365 beaches: one for every day of the year!

ARG.fact: Aconcagua in Argentina is the highest mountain in the Americas, almost 7,000 metres tall.

ARM.fact: Yerevan, Armenia's capital, was founded in 782 BC, so it is older than Rome!

AUS.fact: Kangaroos and koalas live in Australia, and the Great Barrier Reef, the world's biggest coral reef, lies off its coast.

AUT.fact: Mozart, one of the most famous composers of all time, was born in Salzburg, Austria, in 1756.

AZE.fact: Azerbaijan is called the 'Land of Fire': on one hillside, gas seeping out of the ground burns day and night.

BHS.fact: On one island in the Bahamas, pigs swim out to meet the boats! It is called Pig Beach.

BHR.fact: Bahrain is a country of islands, more than 30 of them, joined to Saudi Arabia by a 25 km bridge.

BGD.fact: The Sundarbans in Bangladesh is the biggest mangrove forest in the world, and Bengal tigers live there.

BRB.fact: Flying fish, which glide above the waves on their long fins, are a favourite food in Barbados.

BLR.fact: Belarus has about 11,000 lakes, and wild European bison roam its ancient forests.

BEL.fact: Belgium is famous for chocolate and waffles, and the comic heroes Tintin and the Smurfs were created there.

BLZ.fact: Belize's Great Blue Hole is a giant round sinkhole in the sea, more than 120 metres deep.

BEN.fact: Ganvié in Benin is a whole village built on stilts in a lake. People get around by boat.

BTN.fact: Bhutan measures how happy its people are. It calls this 'Gross National Happiness'.

BOL.fact: Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia is the biggest salt flat in the world. After rain it turns into a giant mirror!

BIH.fact: In Mostar, brave divers jump from a famous old stone bridge into the river more than 20 metres below.

BWA.fact: Botswana has more elephants than any other country: about 130,000 of them.

BRA.fact: Most of the Amazon, the biggest rainforest on Earth, is in Brazil.

BRN.fact: Kampong Ayer in Brunei is a whole town of wooden houses on stilts over a river, with schools and shops too.

BGR.fact: Bulgaria's Rose Valley grows roses for rose oil, which is used in perfumes all over the world.

BFA.fact: Burkina Faso's name means 'land of honest people'.

BDI.fact: Burundi is famous for its royal drummers, who dance while beating huge drums they carry on their heads.

KHM.fact: Angkor Wat in Cambodia is the biggest religious building in the world, and it is on Cambodia's flag.

CMR.fact: Cameroon is called 'Africa in miniature' because it has beaches, deserts, mountains, rainforests and savanna.

CAN.fact: Canada has the longest coastline in the world and more lakes than any other country.

CPV.fact: Cape Verde is a group of volcanic islands in the Atlantic. The volcano on Fogo island last erupted in 2014.

CAF.fact: Forest elephants and western lowland gorillas live in the rainforests of the Central African Republic.

TCD.fact: Chad is named after Lake Chad, a huge lake that has shrunk a lot in the last 60 years.

CHL.fact: Chile is over 4,000 km long but very thin, and its Atacama Desert is one of the driest places on Earth.

CHN.fact: Giant pandas live in China's bamboo forests, and the Great Wall of China is thousands of kilometres long.

COL.fact: Colombia has more kinds of birds than any other country: almost 2,000 different species!

COM.fact: The coelacanth, a fish once thought to have died out with the dinosaurs, lives in the deep sea around Comoros.

CRI.fact: Costa Rica has no army, and about a quarter of the country is protected nature, full of sloths and toucans.

HRV.fact: Croatia has more than 1,000 islands, and Dalmatian dogs are named after its region of Dalmatia.

CUB.fact: The bee hummingbird, the smallest bird in the world, lives only in Cuba. It is about as long as your thumb.

CYP.fact: Cyprus is the third-biggest island in the Mediterranean Sea, and the sun shines there on most days.

CZE.fact: Prague's astronomical clock is over 600 years old and still works: little figures pop out every hour.

CIV.fact: Côte d'Ivoire grows more cocoa beans than any other country, so lots of the world's chocolate starts here.

COD.fact: The okapi, which looks like a mix of a giraffe and a zebra, lives in the wild only in DR Congo.

DNK.fact: LEGO was invented in Denmark. Its name comes from the Danish words 'leg godt', which mean 'play well'.

DJI.fact: Lake Assal in Djibouti is the lowest place in Africa and one of the saltiest lakes on Earth.

DMA.fact: Dominica has a 'Boiling Lake': a flooded crack in a volcano where the water bubbles and steams.

DOM.fact: Santo Domingo, founded in 1496, is the oldest city built by Europeans in the Americas.

TLS.fact: East Timor became independent in 2002, so it is one of the youngest countries in the world.

ECU.fact: Ecuador is named after the equator, which runs through it, and giant tortoises live on its Galápagos Islands.

EGY.fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza is about 4,500 years old, and the River Nile flows through Egypt to the sea.

SLV.fact: El Salvador is the smallest country in Central America, and it has more than 20 volcanoes.

GNQ.fact: Equatorial Guinea is the only country in Africa where Spanish is official. In 2026 it moved its capital to a new city.

ERI.fact: Asmara, Eritrea's capital, has so many colourful old buildings that the whole city is a World Heritage Site.

EST.fact: Estonia is very digital: people can vote online, and Skype was invented there.

SWZ.fact: Eswatini used to be called Swaziland. Its king changed the name in 2018.

ETH.fact: Ethiopia has its own calendar with 13 months, so it is about 7 years 'behind' most of the world!

FJI.fact: Fiji is made of more than 300 islands, and people greet each other with a happy 'Bula!'

FIN.fact: Finland has about 188,000 lakes and around 3 million saunas: more than one for every two people!

FRA.fact: The Eiffel Tower in Paris grows up to 15 cm taller on hot summer days, because metal expands in the heat.

GAB.fact: Almost 90% of Gabon is rainforest, and in Loango National Park elephants and hippos visit the beach!

GMB.fact: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa: a thin strip of land along the Gambia River.

GEO.fact: Georgian is written with its own beautiful, curly alphabet of 33 letters.

DEU.fact: Germany has about 25,000 castles, and fairy tales like Hansel and Gretel were collected there by the Brothers Grimm.

GHA.fact: Lake Volta in Ghana is one of the biggest lakes made by people anywhere in the world.

GRC.fact: The Olympic Games began in ancient Greece almost 2,800 years ago.

GRD.fact: Grenada is called the 'Spice Isle'. It grows lots of nutmeg, and there is a nutmeg on its flag!

GTM.fact: Guatemala was at the heart of the ancient Maya world. Huge Maya pyramids still rise above the jungle at Tikal.

GIN.fact: Guinea is called the 'water tower of West Africa' because big rivers, like the Niger, start in its hills.

GNB.fact: In Guinea-Bissau's Bijagós Islands, rare hippos swim in the salty sea between the islands.

GUY.fact: Guyana's Kaieteur Falls drops 226 metres in one go: about four times the height of Niagara Falls.

HTI.fact: Haiti's Citadelle Laferrière, a huge fortress on top of a mountain, is the biggest fortress in the Americas.

HND.fact: The Maya city of Copán in Honduras has a stone staircase carved with more than 2,000 picture-letters.

HUN.fact: The Rubik's Cube was invented in Hungary in 1974, and Budapest has more than 100 hot springs.

ISL.fact: Iceland has volcanoes, glaciers and hot springs. The word 'geyser' comes from Geysir, a hot spring there.

IND.fact: India has 22 official languages, and the game of chess began there about 1,500 years ago.

IDN.fact: Indonesia has more than 17,000 islands, and Komodo dragons, the biggest lizards on Earth, live there.

IRN.fact: Iran used to be called Persia, and fluffy Persian cats are named after it.

IRQ.fact: Some of the first cities and the first writing in the world began in Iraq, over 5,000 years ago.

IRL.fact: Ireland is called the Emerald Isle because it is so green, and Halloween began there as a festival called Samhain.

ISR.fact: Hebrew is an ancient language that was brought back into everyday use about 130 years ago.

ITA.fact: Italy is shaped like a boot, and pizza as we know it was invented in Naples.

JAM.fact: Jamaica is the home of reggae music and of Usain Bolt, the fastest runner ever timed.

JPN.fact: Japan has more than 14,000 islands, and its bullet trains zoom along at up to 320 km/h.

JOR.fact: Petra in Jordan is a whole city carved into pink rock cliffs more than 2,000 years ago.

KAZ.fact: Kazakhstan is the biggest country with no coast, and the first person to go into space blasted off from there.

KEN.fact: Every year more than a million wildebeest cross between Kenya and Tanzania in the Great Migration.

KIR.fact: Kiribati is the first country to see each New Year, and the only one in all four hemispheres: north, south, east and west.

XKX.fact: Kosovo declared independence in 2008, which makes it one of the youngest countries in Europe.

KWT.fact: The Kuwait Towers look like giant balls on spikes, and two of the balls store water!

KGZ.fact: Most of Kyrgyzstan is mountains. Its flag shows the top of a yurt, the round felt tent of nomads.

LAO.fact: Laos is the only country in Southeast Asia with no coast, and the mighty Mekong River flows through it.

LVA.fact: Riga, Latvia's capital, says it had the first decorated Christmas tree, back in 1510.

LBN.fact: A cedar tree is on Lebanon's flag, and some cedars in its mountains are over 1,000 years old.

LSO.fact: Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa, and all of it is more than 1,000 metres above the sea.

LBR.fact: Liberia became Africa's first republic in 1847. Its capital, Monrovia, is named after a US president.

LBY.fact: Libya is about 90% desert, so it built the 'Great Man-Made River' to pipe water from deep underground.

LIE.fact: To reach the sea from Liechtenstein you have to cross two other countries. Only Uzbekistan is the same!

LTU.fact: Basketball is Lithuania's favourite sport, and Lithuanian is one of the oldest languages still spoken in Europe.

LUX.fact: In 2020 Luxembourg became the first country to make all its buses, trams and trains free for everyone.

MDG.fact: Lemurs live in the wild only on Madagascar, and most of its animals and plants are found nowhere else.

MWI.fact: Lake Malawi has more kinds of fish than any other lake in the world, many of them bright and colourful.

MYS.fact: The rafflesia, one of the biggest flowers in the world, grows in Malaysia's rainforests. It smells like rotting meat!

MDV.fact: The Maldives is the flattest country in the world: its highest point is only about 2.4 metres above the sea.

MLI.fact: The Great Mosque of Djenné in Mali is the biggest building in the world made of mud bricks.

MLT.fact: Malta has stone temples that are older than Egypt's pyramids and England's Stonehenge.

MHL.fact: Long ago, sailors in the Marshall Islands made maps of the ocean waves out of sticks and shells.

MRT.fact: The 'Eye of the Sahara' in Mauritania is a giant ring of rock about 40 km wide, easy to see from space.

MUS.fact: The dodo, a big bird that could not fly, lived only on Mauritius. It died out over 300 years ago.

MEX.fact: Corn was first grown in Mexico about 9,000 years ago, and the Aztecs made drinks out of chocolate.

FSM.fact: On the island of Yap, giant stone discs, some taller than a person, were once used as money.

MDA.fact: Orheiul Vechi in Moldova is a monastery carved into a cliff high above a winding river.

MCO.fact: Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world, and racing cars zoom through its streets every year.

MNG.fact: Mongolia has more horses than people, and many families live in round tents called gers.

MNE.fact: Montenegro means 'black mountain', and its Tara River Canyon is one of the deepest canyons in Europe.

MAR.fact: In Morocco, goats climb argan trees to munch on the fruit!

MOZ.fact: Mozambique's long coast has coral reefs where dugongs, sea turtles and whale sharks swim.

MMR.fact: Myanmar is called the 'Land of Golden Pagodas', and the Shwedagon Pagoda is covered in real gold.

NAM.fact: The Namib is probably the oldest desert in the world, and some of its red sand dunes are over 300 metres tall.

NRU.fact: Nauru is the third-smallest country in the world. It has no official capital: the government works in Yaren.

NPL.fact: Mount Everest, the highest mountain on Earth, is on Nepal's border, and Nepal's flag is the only one that isn't a rectangle.

NLD.fact: About a quarter of the Netherlands is below sea level, and there are more bicycles than people!

NZL.fact: The kiwi, a bird that cannot fly, lives only in New Zealand, and New Zealanders are called 'Kiwis' too.

NIC.fact: Lake Nicaragua is so big it has hundreds of islands, and sharks swim up the river into it from the sea.

NER.fact: Niger is named after the Niger River, and dinosaur bones, like those of Nigersaurus, have been found in its desert.

NGA.fact: Nigeria has more people than any other African country, and its film industry, 'Nollywood', makes thousands of films.

PRK.fact: Mount Paektu, an old volcano on North Korea's border with China, has a crater lake called Heaven Lake.

MKD.fact: Lake Ohrid in North Macedonia is over a million years old, one of the oldest lakes in the world.

NOR.fact: In northern Norway the sun does not set for weeks in summer, and the northern lights dance in winter.

OMN.fact: Oman is famous for frankincense, a sweet-smelling tree sap that people have traded for thousands of years.

PAK.fact: K2, the second-highest mountain in the world, is on Pakistan's border with China.

PLW.fact: Palau has a lake full of millions of jellyfish with stings so weak that people can swim among them.

PSE.fact: Jericho in Palestine is one of the oldest cities in the world: people have lived there for about 11,000 years.

PAN.fact: Ships use the Panama Canal to cross between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans instead of sailing around South America.

PNG.fact: More than 800 languages are spoken in Papua New Guinea, more than in any other country.

PRY.fact: Paraguay's flag has a different picture on each side, and most people there speak both Spanish and Guaraní.

PER.fact: Machu Picchu, an Inca city high in the Andes, is in Peru, and potatoes were first grown there.

PHL.fact: The Philippines has more than 7,600 islands, and the tiny tarsier, with huge round eyes, lives there.

POL.fact: Poland's Wieliczka Salt Mine has an underground chapel carved out of salt, even the chandeliers!

PRT.fact: Portugal makes about half of the world's cork, which comes from the bark of cork oak trees.

QAT.fact: Qatar is a small desert country that sticks out into the sea like a thumb. It hosted the football World Cup in 2022.

COG.fact: Brazzaville faces Kinshasa, DR Congo's capital, across the Congo River. They are two of the closest capitals in the world.

ROU.fact: Bran Castle in Romania is famous as 'Dracula's Castle', and lots of brown bears live in the Carpathian Mountains.

RUS.fact: Russia is the biggest country in the world, with 11 time zones, and its Lake Baikal is the deepest lake on Earth.

RWA.fact: Rwanda is called the 'Land of a Thousand Hills', and mountain gorillas live in its misty volcano forests.

KNA.fact: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest country in the Americas, and green vervet monkeys live on its hills.

LCA.fact: Saint Lucia is said to be the only country named after a woman, and you can drive right into one of its volcanoes!

VCT.fact: Saint Vincent's volcano, La Soufrière, erupted in 2021, and the Grenadines are a chain of more than 30 small islands.

WSM.fact: In 2011 Samoa skipped a whole day, 30 December, when it moved to the other side of the International Date Line.

SMR.fact: San Marino is one of the oldest countries in the world. It is said to have been founded in the year 301.

SAU.fact: Saudi Arabia has the biggest sand desert in the world, the Empty Quarter, and no rivers that flow all year.

SEN.fact: Senegal's Lake Retba is bright pink, thanks to tiny salt-loving algae that live in its water.

SRB.fact: Serbian is written in two alphabets, Cyrillic and Latin, and people use both every day.

SYC.fact: The coco de mer palm in Seychelles has the biggest seed of any plant: it can weigh as much as 25 kg!

SLE.fact: Sierra Leone means 'Lion Mountains'. A Portuguese explorer thought its hills looked like lions.

SGP.fact: Singapore is a city and a country at the same time, and its giant metal 'Supertrees' light up at night.

SVK.fact: Bratislava, Slovakia's capital, is the only capital city that touches two other countries: Austria and Hungary.

SVN.fact: Over half of Slovenia is forest, and its caves are home to the olm, a blind salamander that can live 100 years.

SLB.fact: The Solomon Islands are made of nearly 1,000 islands, with some of the most colourful coral reefs on Earth.

SOM.fact: Somalia has the longest coastline of mainland Africa and more camels than any other country.

ZAF.fact: South Africa has three capital cities, and a flat cloud often covers Cape Town's Table Mountain like a tablecloth.

KOR.fact: The Korean alphabet, Hangul, was invented in 1443 by King Sejong so that everyone could learn to read.

SSD.fact: South Sudan became independent in 2011, which makes it the newest country in the world.

ESP.fact: In the Spanish town of Buñol, thousands of people throw tomatoes at each other every year at La Tomatina!

LKA.fact: Sri Lanka grows some of the world's best-known tea, and every year hundreds of elephants gather at one lake.

SDN.fact: Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt: over 200 of them, built by the ancient kingdom of Kush.

SUR.fact: Suriname is the smallest country in South America, and more than 90% of it is rainforest.

SWE.fact: Every winter a hotel made of ice and snow is built in northern Sweden, and the Nobel Prizes are handed out in Stockholm.

CHE.fact: Switzerland has four national languages and lots of snowy Alps, and it is famous for chocolate, cheese and watches.

SYR.fact: Damascus, the capital of Syria, is one of the oldest cities in the world that people still live in.

STP.fact: São Tomé and Príncipe sits almost on the equator, and Pico Cão Grande is a giant needle of rock poking out of the jungle.

TWN.fact: Bubble tea was invented in Taiwan, and the Taipei 101 tower was the tallest building in the world from 2004 to 2010.

TJK.fact: More than 90% of Tajikistan is mountains, and its Pamir Highway is one of the highest roads in the world.

TZA.fact: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is the highest mountain in Africa, with snow on top even though it is near the equator.

THA.fact: Bangkok's full name is the longest place name in the world, and the elephant is Thailand's national animal.

TGO.fact: In northern Togo, the Batammariba people build tall mud tower houses that look like little castles.

TON.fact: Tonga is the only kingdom left in the Pacific, and it is one of the first countries to see each new day.

TTO.fact: The steelpan drum was invented in Trinidad and Tobago, made from old oil barrels.

TUN.fact: Star Wars scenes were filmed in Tunisia, and Luke Skywalker's home planet is named after the town of Tataouine.

TUR.fact: Istanbul in Turkey is built on two continents, Europe and Asia, and tulips came to Europe from Turkey.

TKM.fact: Turkmenistan's Akhal-Teke horses have shiny coats that gleam like gold or silver in the sun.

TUV.fact: Tuvalu earns money from its internet name, '.tv', which TV companies love to use.

UGA.fact: The River Nile flows out of Lake Victoria in Uganda, and mountain gorillas live in Uganda's misty forests.

UKR.fact: Ukraine is the biggest country completely in Europe, and it grows huge fields of golden sunflowers.

ARE.fact: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world: 828 metres, with 163 floors!

GBR.fact: The United Kingdom is made of four countries: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

USA.fact: The United States has 50 states, and Yellowstone, opened in 1872, was the first national park in the world.

URY.fact: Uruguay hosted the very first football World Cup in 1930, and won it!

UZB.fact: The old Silk Road cities of Samarkand and Bukhara, full of blue-tiled domes, are in Uzbekistan.

VUT.fact: Vanuatu has an underwater post office: divers can post waterproof postcards there!

VAT.fact: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world. It is completely inside the city of Rome.

VEN.fact: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the highest waterfall in the world: the water falls almost 1 km!

VNM.fact: Son Doong in Vietnam is the biggest cave in the world. It is so huge it has its own jungle and clouds inside!

YEM.fact: Socotra, an island of Yemen, has strange 'dragon's blood' trees shaped like giant umbrellas.

ZMB.fact: Victoria Falls, on Zambia's border, is one of the biggest waterfalls on Earth. Locals call it 'the smoke that thunders'.

ZWE.fact: Great Zimbabwe, a city of huge stone walls built about 800 years ago, gave the country its name.

ASM.fact: American Samoa is the only part of the United States south of the equator where people live.

AIA.fact: Anguilla's name may come from the Spanish word for 'eel', because the island is long and thin.

ABW.fact: Aruba's divi-divi trees all lean the same way, because the wind there always blows from one direction.

ATC.fact: No people live on these tiny islands, only seabirds, turtles and sea snakes. They are a protected nature reserve.

BMU.fact: Bermuda has pink sand beaches, coloured by the shells of tiny pink sea creatures.

IOT.fact: The Chagos Islands are tiny coral atolls in the middle of the Indian Ocean, surrounded by very clear seas.

VGB.fact: At The Baths, giant boulders on a beach in the British Virgin Islands make secret pools and caves.

BES.fact: Bonaire, the biggest of these islands, has pink flamingos and some of the best coral reefs in the Caribbean.

CYM.fact: At Stingray City in the Cayman Islands, gentle stingrays swim right up to people in shallow water.

IOA.fact: Every year, millions of red crabs march across Christmas Island to the sea to lay their eggs.

COK.fact: The 15 Cook Islands are spread over an area of ocean about as big as Mexico.

CUW.fact: Willemstad in Curaçao has rainbow-coloured houses and a floating bridge that swings open to let ships through.

FLK.fact: Five kinds of penguins live on the Falkland Islands, and there are far more sheep than people.

FRO.fact: The Faroe Islands have more sheep than people, and their name may mean 'sheep islands'.

GUF.fact: Europe launches its space rockets from French Guiana, because it is close to the equator.

PYF.fact: French Polynesia has 118 islands, including Tahiti and Bora Bora, spread across a huge area of the Pacific.

ATF.fact: No one lives here for good: only scientists, who study the penguins, seals and weather on these windy islands.

GRL.fact: Greenland is the biggest island in the world, and about four-fifths of it is covered by a thick sheet of ice.

GLP.fact: Seen from above, Guadeloupe's two main islands look like the wings of a butterfly.

GUM.fact: Guam is near the Mariana Trench, the deepest place in all the oceans, nearly 11 km down.

HMD.fact: Heard Island has Australia's only active volcanoes and is mostly covered by glaciers. No people live there.

MTQ.fact: Martinique's old name means 'island of flowers', and Mount Pelée, a volcano, rises above its rainforests.

MYT.fact: Mayotte is surrounded by one of the biggest lagoons in the world, where turtles, dolphins and whales swim.

MSR.fact: Montserrat's old capital, Plymouth, was buried by a volcano in the 1990s, so people now live in the north.

NCL.fact: The kagu, a grey bird that barks like a dog, lives only in New Caledonia, around one of the biggest lagoons on Earth.

NIU.fact: Niue is one of the biggest coral islands in the world, and its whole sky is protected for stargazing.

NFK.fact: The Norfolk Island pine, a tree shaped like a Christmas tree, grows wild only on this little island.

MNP.fact: The Northern Mariana Islands are a chain of 14 islands, and some of the northern ones are active volcanoes.

PCN.fact: Fewer than 50 people live on Pitcairn. Many are related to sailors from the famous ship HMS Bounty.

PRI.fact: Puerto Rico has bays that glow blue at night, lit up by tiny glowing sea creatures.

REU.fact: Piton de la Fournaise on Réunion is one of the most active volcanoes in the world.

BLM.fact: Saint Barthélemy once belonged to Sweden, which is why its capital, Gustavia, is named after a Swedish king.

SHN.fact: Saint Helena is one of the most remote islands on Earth, about 2,000 km from Africa. Napoleon died there in 1821.

MAF.fact: Saint Martin shares its island with Sint Maarten: one island, split between France and the Netherlands.

SPM.fact: These small islands near Canada are the last piece of France left in North America.

SXM.fact: At Maho Beach in Sint Maarten, big planes fly just above people's heads as they come in to land.

SGS.fact: South Georgia has huge colonies of king penguins, with hundreds of thousands of birds on a single beach.

TKL.fact: Tokelau has no capital: its three coral atolls take turns leading. It was one of the first places to run on solar power.

TCA.fact: The Turks Islands are named after a cactus with a red top that looks like a Turkish fez hat.

VIR.fact: In the US Virgin Islands, cars drive on the left side of the road, unlike the rest of the United States.

WLF.fact: Wallis and Futuna still has three traditional kings, who rule alongside the French government.

ESH.fact: Western Sahara is mostly desert, and one of the world's longest conveyor belts carries rocks about 100 km to the sea.

ATA.fact: Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth: the lowest temperature ever measured there was −89 °C.

US-AL.fact: The rockets that took astronauts to the Moon were designed in Huntsville, Alabama, nicknamed 'Rocket City'.

US-AK.fact: Alaska is the biggest state, more than twice the size of Texas, and its capital, Juneau, can't be reached by road.

US-AZ.fact: The Grand Canyon in Arizona is about 1.8 km deep. The Colorado River carved it over millions of years.

US-AR.fact: At Crater of Diamonds State Park in Arkansas, visitors can dig for real diamonds and keep what they find!

US-CA.fact: California has more people than any other state, and its redwood trees are the tallest trees on Earth.

US-CO.fact: Denver is called the 'Mile High City' because it sits one mile (1.6 km) above sea level.

US-CT.fact: The world's first telephone book was printed in New Haven, Connecticut, in 1878.

US-DE.fact: Delaware is called 'The First State' because it was the first to approve the US Constitution, in 1787.

US-FL.fact: Florida's Everglades is the only place in the world where alligators and crocodiles live side by side.

US-GA.fact: Georgia is famous for its peaches and peanuts, and Atlanta has one of the biggest aquariums in the world.

US-HI.fact: Hawaii is the only state made up entirely of islands, and its Kilauea volcano is one of the most active on Earth.

US-ID.fact: Idaho grows about a third of all the potatoes in the United States.

US-IL.fact: The world's first skyscraper went up in Chicago, Illinois, in 1885: the ten-storey Home Insurance Building.

US-IN.fact: The Indianapolis 500, one of the world's most famous car races, has been held in Indiana since 1911.

US-IA.fact: Iowa grows more corn than any other state, and it has about seven pigs for every person!

US-KS.fact: Kansas is in the middle of the country: the centre of the 48 joined-up states is near Lebanon, Kansas.

US-KY.fact: Mammoth Cave in Kentucky is the longest known cave system in the world, with more than 680 km of passages.

US-LA.fact: New Orleans, Louisiana, is the birthplace of jazz music.

US-ME.fact: Maine catches most of the lobsters eaten in the United States.

US-MD.fact: The words of the US national anthem, 'The Star-Spangled Banner', were written in Baltimore, Maryland, in 1814.

US-MA.fact: Basketball was invented in Springfield, Massachusetts, in 1891, with peach baskets for hoops.

US-MI.fact: Michigan touches four of the five Great Lakes, and its two big peninsulas are joined by the Mackinac Bridge.

US-MN.fact: Minnesota is called the 'Land of 10,000 Lakes', but it really has more than 11,000!

US-MS.fact: Mississippi is named after the Mississippi River, one of the longest rivers in North America.

US-MO.fact: The Gateway Arch in St. Louis, Missouri, is the tallest arch in the world, at 192 metres.

US-MT.fact: The first Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton ever found was dug up in Montana, in 1902.

US-NE.fact: Kool-Aid, the fruity drink powder, was invented in Hastings, Nebraska, in 1927.

US-NV.fact: Nevada is the driest state in the country, and most of it is desert and mountains.

US-NH.fact: In 1934 a wind gust of 372 km/h was measured on Mount Washington, New Hampshire: a world record for 62 years.

US-NJ.fact: New Jersey has more people for its size than any other state, and Thomas Edison made his famous light bulb there.

US-NM.fact: Santa Fe, founded in 1610, is the highest state capital: more than 2,100 metres above sea level.

US-NY.fact: New York City has more people than any other US city, and the Statue of Liberty stands in its harbour.

US-NC.fact: The Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flight near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, in 1903.

US-ND.fact: North Dakota grows more sunflowers than any other state.

US-OH.fact: Seven US presidents were born in Ohio, and Neil Armstrong, the first person on the Moon, grew up there.

US-OK.fact: Oklahoma is home to 39 Native American tribal nations, more than almost any other state.

US-OR.fact: Crater Lake in Oregon fills an old volcano and is the deepest lake in the United States, almost 600 metres deep.

US-PA.fact: The Declaration of Independence was signed in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, in 1776.

US-RI.fact: Rhode Island is the smallest state, but it has about 640 km of coastline.

US-SC.fact: The palmetto tree on South Carolina's flag honours a fort built of palmetto logs that cannonballs could not break.

US-SD.fact: Mount Rushmore in South Dakota shows four US presidents carved into a mountain, each face about 18 metres tall.

US-TN.fact: Nashville is called 'Music City', and the Great Smoky Mountains are the most visited national park in the US.

US-TX.fact: Texas is the second-biggest state, and from 1836 to 1845 it was its own country: the Republic of Texas.

US-UT.fact: The Great Salt Lake in Utah is so salty that people float in it easily.

US-VT.fact: Vermont makes more maple syrup than any other state, and Montpelier is the smallest state capital.

US-VA.fact: Eight US presidents were born in Virginia, more than in any other state, including George Washington.

US-WA.fact: Washington grows more apples than any other state: about 6 of every 10 apples grown in the US.

US-WV.fact: West Virginia is the only state completely inside the Appalachian Mountains, some of the oldest mountains on Earth.

US-WI.fact: Wisconsin makes more cheese than any other state, and its football fans wear foam 'cheesehead' hats.

US-WY.fact: Most of Yellowstone, the world's first national park, is in Wyoming, which has fewer people than any other state.

US-DC.fact: Washington, D.C. is the capital of the United States. The President lives and works there, in the White House.
